The problem asks us to simulate a process of removing characters from a string $s$ until it becomes empty.
In each operation, we remove the first occurrence of every character from 'a' to 'z' that exists in the current string.
We need to return the string state right before the last operation.

Let's analyze the process.
Suppose the string is $s$.
In one operation, we remove the first 'a', first 'b', ..., first 'z'.
This means if a character appears $k$ times in the string, it will be removed in the $1^{st}, 2^{nd}, \dots, k^{th}$ operations.
Specifically, the $i$-th occurrence of a character $c$ (1-indexed) will be removed in the $i$-th operation.
The process stops when the string is empty. This happens after $M$ operations, where $M$ is the maximum frequency of any character in the original string $s$.
Why? Because the character with the maximum frequency $M$ will have its $M$-th occurrence removed in the $M$-th operation. No character appears more than $M$ times, so no character survives beyond the $M$-th operation.
So the total number of operations is $M = \max(\text{count}(c))$ for $c \in \{'a', \dots, 'z'\}$.

We need to return the string right before the last operation.
The last operation is the $M$-th operation.
So we need the state of the string after $M-1$ operations.
Which characters remain after $M-1$ operations?
A character $c$ remains if it has not been removed in the first $M-1$ operations.
Since the $i$-th occurrence of $c$ is removed in the $i$-th operation, the occurrences that remain after $M-1$ operations are those with index $i > M-1$, i.e., $i \ge M$.
Since the maximum frequency is $M$, the only occurrences that satisfy $i \ge M$ are those where $i = M$.
So, only the characters that appear exactly $M$ times in the original string will contribute to the result. Specifically, only their $M$-th (last) occurrence will remain.
Characters that appear fewer than $M$ times will be completely removed before the $M$-th operation.
Characters that appear $M$ times will have their first $M-1$ occurrences removed in operations $1$ to $M-1$. Their $M$-th occurrence will be removed in the $M$-th operation.
So right before the $M$-th operation, the string consists of the $M$-th occurrence of every character that has frequency $M$ in the original string, preserving their relative order from the original string.
